hero.title: A sound app you don't have to browse
hero.intro: I designed, built and launched SoundLax on my own. It is an ambient sound app for focus, rest and sleep, available on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Mac.

links.text: See it on the App Store

facts.v: Product design, brand, SwiftUI build, launch

p: Before I designed anything, I asked twelve friends one question: what do you listen to while you work?

items: A white noise playlist on Spotify

blocks.text: Four of the twelve used background sound. None of them used a sound app.

p: The need was there, but the apps built for it were not worth opening. People accepted ads and autoplay just to play rain in the background.

The brief I set myself was [[one place to start a sound within a couple of seconds]], without being sold a programme. I was also building it on my own, so every feature had to be something I could design, build and maintain myself.

blocks.title: No library on the home screen
p: Most sound apps open on a grid of hundreds of tracks and a search bar. SoundLax opens on four birds instead, and each one represents a mood: tūī for sharp focus, ruru for deep work, fantail for light and easy, and kererū for relaxing.
People choose how they want to feel, and the sound is already selected for them. {{Is the full sound list one tap away? If so, say so here.}}

blocks.title: No player that disappears
p: In the apps I tested, the playback controls disappeared as soon as I moved to another screen.
In SoundLax, the now-playing bar stays at the bottom of every screen, so changing the mix or stopping a sound takes one tap from anywhere in the app.

image.alt: The same now-playing bar at the bottom of two different SoundLax screens
image.prepare: The bottom third of two different screens side by side (for example Home and Sleep), with the same now-playing bar on both.
image.caption: The same now-playing bar appears on every screen.

blocks.title: No mixer on every screen
p: Some people want to layer rain over café noise and adjust each volume. Most people only want a sound playing.
For that reason, the mixer sits behind a single card, 'Mix your own set', rather than appearing on every screen. It is available to the people who want it and stays out of the way for everyone else.

image.alt: The SoundLax mixer with three sounds layered and their volume sliders
image.prepare: The mixer open with two or three sounds layered (for example Brown Noise, Café Ambience and Soft Piano) and their volume sliders.
image.caption: The mixer opens from one card on the home screen.

p: Many calm apps look calm in the same way: soft gradients, flat illustration, and blue and purple palettes. I wanted SoundLax to have more character and a clear connection to where it was made.

Birdsong is part of everyday life in New Zealand, from suburban gardens to native bush, so native birds were a natural starting point. I paired vintage naturalist illustrations with [[bold colour, subtle grain and a clean, modern interface]].
Each bird also represents a mood, so the illustrations work as navigation as well as decoration.

items.text: When I was working or doing housework, I used to search YouTube for background music and often lose 30 minutes doing it. That doesn't happen with this app.
items.source: App Store review, Japan (translated) {{check the translation}}

items.text: It actually wakes me up like a civilized human being, unlike the default Apple alarm which sounds like a localized nuclear siren designed to trigger a fight-or-flight response.
The sound quality is lovely, especially the rain and nature tracks, and the overall experience feels polished and easy to use.
I just really wish it could auto-save any tweaks I made to existing mixes so they will be ready next time without me having to manually readjust.

p: Not all of the feedback was positive. People asked for more sounds and better balance between them, and several people noticed that Brown Noise cut out briefly each time it looped, first on the Mac version.

p: The project also gave me responsibility for a whole product for the first time: the early research with friends, the design, building it in SwiftUI with AI assistance, App Store review, subscriptions, and fixing bugs that users found before I did.

blocks.heading: What I'd do differently
p: {{One specific thing. A candidate: test every sound loop on every device before launch, since people found the Brown Noise cut before I did. Keep it only if it's true for you.}}
